utility.notes: SCE's own 'Incorporated Cities and Counties Served by SCE' fact sheet (updated 3/17/2025) explicitly lists 'Norco' by name among the cities in its service area.

generation_supplier.notes: Norco is a named member city of Western Community Energy (WCE), but WCE deregistered with the CPUC and dissolved via Chapter 9 bankruptcy in 2021, with customers involuntarily returned to their default IOU. No currently-operating CCA was confirmed serving Norco this session, so left null rather than recording a defunct relationship as active.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Southern California Edison (SCE), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by SCE across its entire distribution territory, which includes Norco/Riverside County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for other SCE-territory records this session, reused as a utility-level fact.

value.name: California Contractor's State License (wallet card) or property owner proof of identification
Current City of Norco Business License (contractors, including all subcontractors)

SolarAPP+ training completion certificate (IREC's 'How to Use SolarAPP+ For Rooftop Solar Projects,' or the storage-specific version if including batteries) — required once, before first SolarAPP+ submission

required_documents.notes: The general contractor/owner paperwork requirements apply to all Norco permits including solar; the SolarAPP+ training certificate requirement is specific to the online SolarAPP+ application option described on this same page.

timeline_days.notes: Search-engine synthesis indicates a building permit is valid for 180 days after issuance, but a review/approval timeline itself was not confirmed.

value.program_or_pathway: Standard building permit; certain systems SolarApp+-eligible
other_conditions: Solar panels must be integral with the roof slope and design of the building
Aluminum frames for roof-mounted solar panels are prohibited unless completely hidden from ground-level view
